body:
Left a few comments about implementation details, but overall looks great. The only serious comment I have is about removing multiple model support, because this is already a pretty key part of the plugins used most frequently in the extension by default (gpt3.5 for summarization, gpt4 for everything more important). My idea on this is something like "model roles."

Since it should be possible to literally use _only_ a local model for everything, the calls to sdk.models.gpt35 can't stay. But unfortunately we also can't postpone the ability to call a faster/cheaper model. The solution seems to be able to "fall back" to the default model, but provide a property for customization. For example, the config could look like this:
```python
config = ContinueConfig(
...
  models: Models(
    default=OpenAI("gpt4",...),
    small=OpenAI("gpt-3.5",...),
    large=None,  # This would fall back to the default model (these are all optional kwargs, except default)
    custom={ "my-custom-model-name", MyCustomModel(...), ... }
  )
)
  ```
  
  I like this solution because it:
  1. Maintains strong typing on the sdk.models.
  2. Lets people add whatever models they want without having to modify the Models class
  3. Lets us keep the common functionality of using a smaller model for simpler tasks like summarization
  
Note that doing this would require using an async "start"/"initialize" method on the Models class, instead of a "create" classmethod, but this feels like a fair tradeoff.

I'm leaning towards a different version of a), or could be a mixture of a) and b), something like this

I lean towards a) because it lets LLMs declaratively ask for what they want, specifically, rather than giving them access to all secrets through the SDK function

```python
class OpenAI(LLM):
    def wanted_permissions(self):
        # a) return desired privileged information
        return {"secrets": ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]}
        
        # a and b) return desired sdk method
        return {"methods": ["get_user_secret"]}
    
    async def start(self, privileged):
        # a) sdk takes care of giving llm the secret
        privileged.secrets["OPENAI_API_KEY"]
        # b) sdk returns wanted method
        await privileged.sdk.get_user_secret("OPENAI_API_KEY") # special sdk object, other methods raise AttributeError
```

body:
This is an interesting question in terms of replacement. On one hand, the idea is to decrease amount of hardcoded models on the steps, so that users can switch to anything. On the other, model upgrades may be wanted based on context size...

I don't know if `sdk.models.large` would be a good replacement here unless we explicitly define "large" as a model that is "actually large in size, expensive" **and** "has a large context size compared to the current models" (that latter part being something that should be documented, in my opinion. it would be a footgun if someone sets their `large` model to something smaller in context to `model_to_use`).

One possible avenue to this is letting the LLM object decide if it should upgrade in the background, letting the user decide if that's behavior they want to have. I can see a future where someone does not want to use any OpenAI models, ever, and they want to upgrade from LLaMA-2 to [LLongMA-13B](https://huggingface.co/conceptofmind/LLongMA-13b) in the cases where the context is too large to warrant an upgrade.

One drawback of that is most likely we'd always blow past the normal context window and use the long model, which for the case of an OpenAI user it'd mean a giant hole in their wallet.

Maybe `model_to_use = await model_to_use.maybe_upgrade()` would be a valid compromise. Let's LLMs decide the upgrade path, while only letting specific steps that desire large context windows signal that to the LLM.

body:
This looks like the really important part!

There's a high-level thing that I want to point out right away. It's critical to make sure that every sub-class of LLM has the same interface, and it would probably require changing something here to give it access to the SDK to call tools.

So the first thing I might think is that you could find a way to keep a lot of this logic inside of the OpenAIAgent class and just call the SDK from inside of a step. But the question then becomes: how do we pass the output of the tools back into the assistant?

It might actually be possible to do the following in a Step: [call stream_chat] -> [get response] -> [call tool based on response (in the Step, not OpenAIAgent)] -> [pass results of tool back as the input to another stream_chat call] -> [repeat].

The important thing is to make sure that no "state" is stored in the LLM class, so that it can be called multiple times without worrying about what previous calls did. I think the key to this is creating a new thread for each stream_chat call, and making separate stream_chat calls whenever a tool is invoked

I was using mixtrail in continue and asked `merge the regex in the 2 replaces and then explain yourself isoString.replace(/[-:]/g, "").replace(/\.\d+Z/, "");`

it responded..

Sure, you can chain the two replace() methods together like this:
```
return isoString.replace(/[-:.\d+Z]/g, "");
```

This regular expression (/[-:.\d+Z]/g) matches any of the characters -, :, ., +, or Z that appear in the ISO string, and the g flag at the end of the expression tells it to do this for all occurrences of the matched characters, not just the first one.

This will remove all -, :, ., +, and Z characters from the ISO string, leaving only the digits that represent the date and time.

even though after some struggle I understand that this either sets mentions or slash_commands to the candidates variable, it is very unclear on the first glance. It seems like candidates must be bool. I'd change it to something more obvious and add proper typing. For example:

```
-- Function to get completion items
--- @param prefix string
--- @return CompletionItem[]
function M.get_completion_items(prefix)
  ---@type CompletionItem[]
  local items = {}
  ---@type CompletionItem[]
  local candidates = {}
  if prefix:sub(1, 1) == '@' then
    candidates = M.mentions
  elseif prefix:sub(1, 1) == '/' then
    candidates = M.slash_commands
  end

  for _, item in ipairs(candidates) do
    -- if vim.startswith(item.word, prefix) then
    table.insert(items, {
      word = vim.startswith(item.word, prefix) and item.word or (prefix .. item.word),
      kind = item.kind,
      menu = item.menu,
      user_data = { has_submenu = item.has_submenu },
    })
    -- end
  end

  return items
end
```

And in general will be very useful to see better typing across this code, makes it much easier to understand.

body:
See: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

_Cache hits require 100% identical prompt segments, including all text and images up to and including the block marked with cache control. The same block must be marked with cache_control during cache reads and creation._

So it needs the marker both to retrieve the previous cache (so in the exact same place as the previous request), as well as to mark up to when the request should be cached now. (creation)

This is also how it's done in the 'Continuing a multi-turn conversation' example on their page.

If provider=`azure` works properly, then `apiType` could be eliminated, and `apiVersion` can use your default. Not so with `engine`.

As of this week, if I set `provider` to "azure", it generates the wrong URL:  Prior to this week, it used the `engine` to name the _deployment_ and get my endpoint. Now it uses `model`, which is incorrect.

The deployment name is part of my URL, presumably to manage multiple instances of the same model. So I think the `azure` provider must have a way to capture my deployment name. I'm not sure what `engine` was supposed to be, but it used to serve the role of putting my _deployment_ name in the proper place in the URL.  

Lacking `engine` (or `deployment`), then `model` is a good default, but we need a way to specify it.

The `useWebviewListener("setTTSNative")` handler's mixed return types (`true`, `false`, or a `Promise`) can cause inconsistent behavior, making it harder to handle. Standardizing the return type to always be a `Promise` or whatever is ideal ensures predictability and simplifies integration, reducing potential bugs and improving maintainability.

The `Promise` in `setTTSNative` lacks explicit error handling, which could result in uncaught errors during unexpected failures. Try wrapping the logic in a `try-catch` block to ensure errors are logged and handled.

body:
> Additional note: I changed both qwen and codestral template so that they produce a single prompt instead of separate prefix and suffix.
> Explanation:
> Creating prefix and suffix will result in a request that has "prompt" and "suffix" in the request body. However, after all, the model itself has to get a single prompt (because LLM models only have one "prompt" as input), so somewhere in the process, the provided "prompt" and "suffix" parameters will be converted to a single "prompt", but may not in a way we want: in case of codestral it's [SUFFIX]{suffix}[PREFIX]{prefix}, that makes it impossible to put the context before the [PREFIX] and [SUFFIX] separators. In contrast, providing a single prompt will let us achieve this format: {context}[PREFIX]{prefix}[SUFFIX]{suffix}

Update: I found that this change is conceptually wrong, I updated the PR to contain only minimal changes to the template. With other modifications it's working quite well already.

Current changes in the codestral template:
- Now it uses relative instead of absolute file paths in the context
- Added "++++" as a stop word because this is used in the prompt to mark new files

body:
@Patrick-Erichsen  Created a .prompt file for my team that works pretty reliable with llama3.3 and GPT-4o. Still have to battle test and benchmark it.

______________________________________________________________


name: Unified Diff Generator
description: Guide for generating clean, applicable unified diffs
---

Act as an expert software developer who specializes in creating precise unified diffs. When given code modification requests, you will respond with clean, applicable unified diff patches that can be directly applied to the codebase.

## Unified Diff Format

```diff
--- original/path/file.ext
+++ modified/path/file.ext
@@ -1,7 +1,7 @@
 unchanged line
 unchanged line
 unchanged line
-removed line
+added line
 unchanged line
 unchanged line
 unchanged line
```

## Key Guidelines

1. **Hunk Structure**:
   - Start each segment of changes with `@@ start_line_before,lines_count_before start_line_after,lines_count_after @@`
   - Only include hunks with actual changes (containing `+` or `-` lines)
   - Sart every unchanged line with an additional space ` `
   - There should be 3 unchanged lines before and after any changes.
   - If there are less than 3 lines before or after the changes include only the available or non if at the start or end of the file.

2. **Code Blocks**:
   - When modifying a function, method, or block, replace the entire block
   - Remove the old version with `-` lines
   - Add the new version with `+` lines
   - This ensures syntactic correctness and proper indentation

3. **File Operations**:
   - To move code within a file: create two hunks (one for deletion, one for insertion)

4. **Patch Correctness**:
   - Verify that diffs apply cleanly against current file contents
   - Maintain proper indentation in all added/modified code
   - Ensure syntactic correctness in the resulting code

## Examples

### Example 1: File modification with only one function
```diff
--- app/utils.py
+++ app/utils.py
@@ -1,3 +1,5 @@
-def calculate_total(items):
-    total = 0
-    for item in items:
-        total += item.price
-    return total
+def calculate_total(items, discount=0):
+    total = sum(item.price for item in items)
+    return total * (1 - discount/100)
```

### Example 2: Import Addition
```diff
--- app/models.py
+++ app/models.py
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 import pandas
 import datetime
 import json
+import uuid
 from typing import Dict, List, Optional
 
 def main():
```

### Example 4: Moving Code Within a File and Modifying Multi Parts in the File 
```diff
--- app/views.py
+++ app/views.py
@@ -12,23 +12,18 @@
         return False
     return True
 
-def validate_input(data):
-    """Validate user input."""
-    if not data.get('name'):
-        return False
-    return True
 
 def main():
     """Main function."""
@@ -64,70 +64,76 @@
 class UserController:
     """Handle user-related operations."""
     
+    def validate_input(data):
+        """Validate user input."""
+        if not data.get('name'):
+            return False
+        return True
+    
     def create_user(self, data):
         """Create a user."""
         print(data)
```

## Best Practices

1. **Think Carefully Before Generating**:
   - Understand the complete request
   - Consider dependencies and imports
   - Identify all files that need modification

2. **Quality Assurance**:
   - Verify all necessary modifications are included
   - Check that indentation is preserved
   - Ensure syntactic correctness

Remember that your unified diffs will be applied directly to code, so precision and correctness are essential.
Always generate diffs that will apply cleanly and produce working, syntactically correct code.

Submitted this to the @tomasz-stefaniak oracle (e.g. Clean Code assistant)

**Prompt**
```ts core/config/load.ts (667-669)
    slashCommands: final.slashCommands?.map(
      ({ run, ...slashCommandDescription }) => slashCommandDescription,
    ),
```
```ts
slashCommands: final.slashCommands?.map((s) => ({
name: s.name,
description: s.description,
params: s.params, // TODO: is this why params aren't referenced properly by slash commands?
}))
```
which version is cleaner?

---

**Response**
The first version using destructuring is cleaner and more maintainable for several reasons:

```ts core/config/load.ts
slashCommands: final.slashCommands?.map(
  ({ run, ...slashCommandDescription }) => slashCommandDescription,
),
```

Advantages of the first version:
1. It uses object destructuring with rest parameters (`...`) to explicitly show we're removing the `run` property while keeping everything else
2. It's more maintainable - if new properties are added to slash commands in the future, they'll automatically be included without modifying this code
3. It follows the Open/Closed Principle better - the code is open for extension (new properties) but closed for modification
4. It's more concise and has less repetition

The second version:
```ts
slashCommands: final.slashCommands?.map((s) => ({
  name: s.name,
  description: s.description,
  params: s.params,
}))
```

Has these drawbacks:
1. It explicitly lists every property that needs to be copied
2. It's more brittle - if new properties are added, this code needs to be updated
3. More verbose and repetitive
4. Higher chance of human error when maintaining the property list

The first version is the better choice as it's more maintainable, flexible, and follows SOLID principles better. It also makes it very clear that we're intentionally excluding the `run` property while preserving everything else.

----

I made the update mostly stylistically but I think I agree with the points made by the model.

Breaking change: The compileChatMessages function's return type has been changed from ChatMessage[] to an object, but it's used in multiple places across the codebase (core/llm/index.ts, core/core.ts, test files) that expect the original ChatMessage[] return type. This will cause type errors and runtime failures in code that directly uses the returned array without destructuring. For example, in core/llm/index.ts line 748, the function result is directly returned without handling the new object structure.

body:
Thank you for your suggestion to move the llama.cpp reranking implementation to the packages/openai-adapters package to better align with the project's architecture.

I initially tried to fully migrate the implementation, but encountered integration issues with the core module that resulted in runtime errors ("Failed to rerank retrieval results TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined"). The reranking functionality has complex integration with the BaseLLM class and retrieval pipeline that made a complete migration challenging without broader refactoring.

To address this while respecting your architectural guidance, I've implemented a hybrid approach:

1. I've maintained the working implementation in the core module (core/llm/llms/LlamaCpp.ts) to preserve functionality.

2. I've added a well-documented LlamaCppApi class in the packages/openai-adapters package that properly extends OpenAIApi, following the established pattern of other adapters.

3. I've updated the constructLlmApi function to use this new LlamaCppApi class for the llama.cpp provider.

In the future, a more comprehensive refactoring could fully migrate the implementation, but that would require changing how the core module interacts with adapters - which seems beyond the scope of the current PR.

Would this approach be acceptable as an intermediate step toward the architectural goal you suggested?
author: fradav

body:
@fradav I really appreciate the thoughtfulness here. I think it's closer to working than it might appear—probably if you were to set up a debugger it would become obvious where the "Cannot read properties of undefined..." is coming from. Would you be willing to investigate this? As far as I know from our other openai-adapters integrations, this should be able to work without much further adjustment

We won't be willing to merge this PR until the code is in the correct spot in openai-adapters, otherwise it is going to make this untestable and harder to maintain down the road

body:
@chezsmithy this will be a great problem to solve, has been on my mind recently. 

The main issue and reason I hadn't approached this yet is that (correct me if I'm wrong) if the user cancels streaming in Agent mode with this implementation after several turns of the conversation, there will be no recent user messages and it will essentially truncate to the beginning of the convo since the pattern is 
user -> assistant + calls -> tool -> assistant + calls -> tool -> assistant + calls etc.

In this case we also can't just truncate back to the last tool message because (if I remember right) e.g. Anthropic won't accept the handshake user -> assistant + calls -> tool (= user in anthropic/gemini) -> user because of sequential user messages

Would love ideas/brainstorming on how to solve this!

Potential runtime error: The code assumes abortController is always defined, but as a newly added parameter with no default value, it could be undefined/null. The function signature uses destructured parameters ({ llm, ide, abortController }) which violates the SlashCommand interface contract. This is ok for now but long-term it's better to avoid importing implementation details from sibling services. This makes it easy to create circular dependencies, which will eventually lead to bugs and are often difficult to resolve.

For example, someone else could, in the future, import implementation details from `nextEdit` into autocomplete and it generate a circular dependency that way.

It's usually better to move the reusable elements to a third directory that both siblings import from.

body:
Clean implementation!

Some changes in mind:
1. Use the existing `files/closed` or `files/opened` messages rather than introducing a new `onDidCloseTextDocument` callback and `initializeOpenedFileCache` message. "files/closed" is already set up for both vs code and jetbrains. It seems like in this implementation, `recentlyEdited` is for open files and `recentlyOpened` is for closed files, but `recentlyOpened` is also initialized with open files. Let's talk about this naming and review the snippet priority. I think recently edited should be prioritized over recently closed. Also, let's implement the existing `files/opened` message rather than adding a new `initializeOpenedFileCache` message. It seems like those should be added to the recently edited cache on startup, not the recently "opened" (closed) cache. 
2. Use URIs all the way through, don't use "file://", will cause bugs, just use uri.toString() in the IDE side . Note that `helper.filepath` was named before we transitioned to URIs, bit misleading
3. Let's add unit tests for the formatting and ranking, especially around the math stuff!

I also wanted to talk to you about snippet ranking, deduplication, and file read latency, can chat in person, you probably already tested this enough but wanted to get a grasp on it. Did we consider storing the actual file contents in the cache? Might not be up to date but would be much faster and these are for "closed" files. Files are often large, is there a concern of recently closed files always filling the remainder of snippet context window?

Were the additions/changes to manual-testing-sandbox intentional? Fine to be included, just checking

EDIT:
after talking with @adarshramiyer feedback has changed to
1. Use the existing "files/closed" message rather than a `onDidCloseTextDocument` callback (partly so works with jetbrains), move logic to core files/closed
2. Instead of a `initializeOpenedFileCache` message, send a "files/opened" message on init, switch onDidChangeActive to using the "files/opened"
4. Rip out the recentlyEditedFiles cache since it's duplicate

body:
I'm coming at this review with the lens of "if we add it now, we'll have to support it forever (or go through a deliberate deprecation process)". I'm worried there are a large number of options here that aren't going to be relevant forever, or that they might not be the final form of this configuration.

It would be helpful to better understand whether all of the cacheUserMessages, cacheAssistantMessages, etc. are truly necessary for people to customize, or whether we just need to set a more sensible default. For example, I'd be curious what values you set here and whether you think we should just ship those as the defaults for everyone. Usage patterns in Continue are probably similar across a variety of users. Not that we couldn't eventually also allow this customization, but it might save a lot of maintenance (and give many users money back without needing to configure anything)

body:
as for me, i think we just need to cache everything we can to cache, since it is saves users money. but main problem with Anthropic, that 5m cache and 1h cache cost differently and 1h cache cost double [pricing](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#pricing). 

I think about 3 possible routes/options:
1. Cache everything and give user minimal control 5m/1h cache (while inside code if user selecting 1h, we automatically adding headers)
2. Give user to control what he want to cache (but from my experience more cached - less expensive when i need to work a lot within same session with huge context) and do not want keep me in 5m time frame.
3. maybe implement custom provider configuration block, which are extending basic configuration per AI provider if necessary. 

i think caching last 2 messages is more than enough default for any type, since cache LRU based (if i got Anthropic docs right)
